coverage.note: This dogfood map binds the crawler policy and the new Skill Packs surface to inspected repository evidence. It is not a whole-site ranking or indexing certification.

evidence.summary: The repository robots policy explicitly allows OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User and general crawlers. This is an implementation fact only; it does not prove crawl frequency, indexing or citation.

instances.note: Crawler access is necessary for some discovery paths but is not a ranking signal or recommendation guarantee.

evidence.summary: The Skill Packs page explicitly describes the output as a portable instruction file, says tool-specific installation differs, and rejects both universal one-click installation and ranking-shortcut framing.
The content policy defines Skill Packs as reusable representations of trusted canonical protocols and explicitly separates product capability from search ranking or AI recommendation claims.

instances.note: Absence is scoped to the reviewed Skill Packs implementation and policy, not every future third-party description of Brali.

relations.rationale: Brali keeps machine access open while avoiding claims that a machine-readable skill file itself creates search or recommendation preference.

knownUnknowns: The map does not establish Google ranking, indexing, AI Overview inclusion, AI Mode inclusion or preferred-source treatment.
The map does not establish ChatGPT citation frequency, ranking or correctness for Brali pages.
The map does not establish that any user has copied, saved, installed or repeatedly used a Brali Skill Pack.
The current implementation changes the trusted entry indexing contract, but legacy zone and cross-domain migration cleanup remain separate work and must not be treated as completed by this map.
No causal search or recommendation outcome is attributed to these patterns until an external measurement design supports that claim.
